step1_analysis.circuit_type: Analog Equalizer Interpolator / Variable Gain Amplifier
step1_analysis.description: A bipolar differential interpolator stage used in an adaptive cable equalizer. It steers a tail current between two differential pairs (fast and slow paths) based on a control voltage, blending their outputs to compensate for frequency-dependent cable loss.

paper_reference.title: A 10 Gb/s BiCMOS Adaptive Cable Equalizer

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the interpolator stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_tail = 1.8V * 1mA = 1.8mW. (Note: The 350mW reported in the paper is for the entire chip including CDR and output buffers).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on a standard 1mA tail current for a high-speed differential pair in a 1.8V supply.

voltage_gain.description: Low-frequency differential voltage gain of the active path.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm * R_load. For I_tail = 1mA, Ic = 0.5mA, gm = Ic/Vt = 19.2mS. With R_load = 1kOhm, Gain = 19.2 V/V = 25.6 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using standard bipolar transconductance at room temperature with 1kOhm load resistors.

bandwidth_3db.description: The frequency at which the AC voltage gain drops by 3 dB from its low-frequency value.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2 * pi * R_load * C_total). Assuming C_total ~ 15fF (Cjc + load parasitics), BW = 1 / (2 * pi * 1k * 15f) = 10.6 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the RC time constant at the output nodes. A 1kOhm resistor and small parasitic capacitances yield a bandwidth in the 10 GHz range.

transient_swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential output voltage swing for a small-signal high-frequency input.

sky130_expected.calculation: For a 20mVpp differential input, Output Swing = 20mV * 19.2 V/V = 384mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Verifies the time-domain large-signal behavior and ensures the stage does not clip prematurely.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, -3dB bandwidth, and transient output swing of the equalizer interpolator stage.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Adaptive Cable Equalizer Interpolator Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Generic NPN model for simulation (since netlist uses 'npn')
.model npn npn(is=1e-16 bf=100 cje=10f cjc=10f)

* DUT
I1 E_TAIL GND 1m
Q1 VEQ_P VFAST_N E_LEFT npn
Q2 E_RIGHT VCONTROL_N E_TAIL npn
Q3 E_LEFT VCONTROL_P E_TAIL npn
Q4 VEQ_N VFAST_P E_LEFT npn
Q5 VEQ_P VSLOW_P E_RIGHT npn
Q6 VEQ_N VSLOW_N E_RIGHT npn
R1 VDD VEQ_P 1k
R2 VDD VEQ_N 1k

* Biasing and Sources
VVDD VDD GND 1.8
VVCONTROL_P VCONTROL_P GND 1.2
VVCONTROL_N VCONTROL_N GND 0.6

* Inputs (Fast path active, Slow path AC grounded)
VFAST_P VFAST_P GND dc 0.9 ac 0.5 sin(0.9 0.01 1G)
VFAST_N VFAST_N GND dc 0.9 ac -0.5 sin(0.9 -0.01 1G)
VSLOW_P VSLOW_P GND dc 0.9 ac 0
VSLOW_N VSLOW_N GND dc 0.9 ac 0

.control
* DC Analysis
op
let power = -i(VVDD)*1.8
print power
meas dc power_meas param power

* AC Analysis
ac dec 100 1Meg 100Gig
let vout_diff = v(VEQ_P) - v(VEQ_N)
let gain_db = vdb(vout_diff)
meas ac low_freq_gain find gain_db at=1Meg
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db='low_freq_gain-3' fall=1

* Transient Analysis
tran 10p 5n
let vout_diff_tran = v(VEQ_P) - v(VEQ_N)
meas tran vout_max max vout_diff_tran from=2n to=5n
meas tran vout_min min vout_diff_tran from=2n to=5n
let tran_swing = vout_max - vout_min
print tran_swing

quit
.endc
